leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer optical lattice clocks for Katori and Ye alone. All four rest the case on the magic-wavelength scheme, performance near 1e-18 beyond the caesium definition of the second, independent reproduction in several laboratories, and the cleanest two-name credit boundary on the shortlist. They agree the citation should be framed around the lattice scheme, not optical clocks in general, so as to separate it from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize. They differ in emphasis: Kroll weighs the step change in measurement capability and calls the timing apt, while Lindroth, in contrast to Kroll, would not lean on the pending redefinition of the second in the citation. Olsson and Pearce each moved to B010 from another opening first choice (aberration-corrected electron microscopy and IceCube respectively) after reading the other ballots. Not shared: the supporters do not agree on how the pending redefinition should weigh, and none resolves the weight of Katori's proposal against Ye's accuracy programme. Kroll discloses a possible connection to the Boulder environment (see flags).

Three members prefer topological insulators with the same trio, Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and cite the same chain of Z2 prediction followed by HgTe edge-channel observation. They describe the interpretation as stable after fifteen years or more and the field as confirmed across many materials. Mehlig treats the recognition as conceptually overdue, a reclassification of insulators by a topological invariant instead of a broken symmetry, while Eriksson and Johansson stress the stability of the interpretation. They are united in flagging the same two weaknesses: the absent Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (Zhang cannot be recognised) and possible overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize. Johansson has moved from circuit QED (B041) and names B046 as his first alternative if the B047 allocation cannot be settled; Eriksson and Mehlig keep B051 as an alternative. Not shared: whether Hasan's three-dimensional work belongs in this prize or a later one.

One member, Danielsson, prefers magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene for MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, as a prediction (2011) followed by experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states (2018). B051 is not the explicit first preference of any other member, though it appears as an alternative for Eriksson, Kroll, Mehlig and Pearce and Danielsson counts a broad base of rankings in the opening ballots. Danielsson himself concedes that the pairing mechanism is unsettled and that Cao, the first author of the 2018 experiments, is outside the three names, and lists B047 and B010 as the safer, more mature options. Danielsson also says he would not oppose B047 if its attribution can be settled.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members agree that the final configuration should be a prediction or invention backed by independent confirmation, and that B010, B047 and B051 are the three serious candidates; no member prefers a candidate outside those three.

Every statement from the B010 supporters and the B047 supporters treats the other's candidate as a respectable alternative, not a rejected one; Kroll says he would not oppose B047 on merit, Mehlig says he would not oppose B010 as a part of a two-part prize, and Danielsson would not oppose B047.

Several members, from different preferred candidates (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce), say that B041 (circuit QED) is a poor choice this year because of the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits and because Girvin and Huang are omitted from the three names.

Katori and Ye is the only pair proposed for B010, and Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is the trio proposed by every B047 supporter; the dispute about names is on the margin (Hasan, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang), not about the core.

Members across the three leading positions say that the citation wording will do real work in answering overlap objections: the lattice scheme for B010, and the Z2 invariant and time-reversal-symmetric edge physics for B047.
scientific_disputes: Whether a precision-measurement invention (B010) counts as a discovery of the same weight as a new organising concept in matter (B047) or a new regime of matter (B051). Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce weigh measurement capability; Danielsson and Eriksson say that precision on its own does not outrank new physics, and Mehlig calls B047 a conceptual change, not an advance.

Whether the 2005 prize (frequency comb) and the 2012 prize (ion control) leave room for a lattice-clock prize. The B010 supporters say the magic-wavelength scheme is a distinct route, since many neutral atoms are interrogated at once; Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig say the toolbox was already recognised.

Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions leaves room for a separate prize on the Z2 insulator and the quantum spin Hall state. Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig argue the time-reversal-invariant, spin-orbit-driven case is distinct; Olsson and Kroll cite 2016 as a risk.
Whether the unsettled superconducting pairing mechanism in B051 makes it too early, or whether the prize honours the observed correlated and superconducting phases, as Danielsson argues.
attribution_disputes: B047: whether Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal; Zhang is deceased) can be acknowledged without extending the three names, and whether Molenkamp can carry the experimental credit alone. Danielsson would put Hasan in place of Mele; Johansson and Mehlig reject dropping Mele because the Kane-Mele papers are joint; Eriksson prefers Mele to Hasan as the origin of the Z2 invariant.

B010: how to weigh Katori's proposal and first realisation against Ye's accuracy programme, and whether ion-clock groups and other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Derevianko) fall outside a two-name credit. Kroll and Lindroth say the committee need not rank the two; no member has shown that a different pair is better.

B051: Cao, the first author of the 2018 experiments, and other experimental groups are outside the three names, and earlier moire-band theory exists. Danielsson would word the citation as a discovery of the states, not as an exhaustive credit.
Several members state that they rely on recollection of priority history, not on verified documentation (Johansson, Kroll, Olsson, Danielsson).
maturity_disputes: B010: the performance is confirmed in many laboratories, and Kroll and Lindroth read the timing as good. Olsson raises whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the second; Kroll and Lindroth say the science does not depend on it and that it should not be leaned on in the citation.

B047: the interpretation has been stable for fifteen years or more, but Mehlig, Eriksson and Johansson all say the allocation is not settled, so maturity of the science is not in dispute while maturity of the credit is.

B051: observation is reproduced by many groups, but the pairing mechanism is debated, and Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Kroll describe the field as early in interpretation, while Danielsson says earlier prizes honoured observed phenomena before full explanation.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers; directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology; co-authors with Delsing, Wilson and Frisk Kockum) discloses a direct connection to B041 and a looser one to B046, would recuse from any decision placing circuit QED in the prize, and has lowered its weight.

Kroll discloses a doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, adjacent to but not part of the B010 credit, and asks the committee to judge whether this requires recusal on B010; he also notes a general proximity to the quantum-information candidates (B046, B041, B058) through his WACQT role.

Olsson discloses professional proximity to transmission electron microscopy (B039) and would recuse from any decision on it; Olsson also notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, relevant to a conflict check on B041.
Eriksson discloses that his research area (DFT and DMFT) is close to B018, his opening first choice, and to the band-theory side of B047, and will not advocate B018 beyond the evidence.

Pearce (chair) discloses that astroparticle physics is adjacent to B061 (IceCube), the candidate he moved away from, and would stand back from any final decision on it. No specific conflict is stated by Danielsson, Lindroth or Mehlig; Lindroth notes only that clock physics is close to atomic structure.
questions_for_round2: For B010: can the committee frame the citation around the magic-wavelength lattice so that it is clearly distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and do Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig accept that distinction as meeting their novelty objection?

For B047: what exact trio or set of names does each B047 supporter propose, how should Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal be handled in citation wording, and is there a form of the allocation that Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce, who have not endorsed a trio, could accept?

How should the committee weigh a measurement-capability achievement (B010) against a new conceptual classification (B047), and does any member hold that this weighting alone should decide between them?

For B047: what specific argument shows that the Z2 insulator and quantum spin Hall effect are separate from the 2016 prize on topological phases, and who among the members who raised the overlap (Olsson, Kroll, Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig) finds it sufficient?

For B051: if a condensed-matter prize is preferred, would Danielsson accept a citation that honours the observed correlated and superconducting states without asserting a pairing mechanism, and how should the omission of Cao be recorded?
Does any member hold that a two-part configuration, as Mehlig raises, combining B047 with B010 would be fairer than a single prize, and if so with what split of credit and which citations?

Given the disclosures of Kroll (B010), Johansson and Olsson (B041, B039), should any member withhold a vote on a specific part of the final configuration, and does this change the count behind any leading position?
summary.chair_observation: In the round-1 files, four members explicitly prefer B010, three prefer B047 and one prefers B051; the two larger groups each name a different scientific criterion (clean attribution and confirmed measurement versus conceptual novelty), and the supporters of each treat the other as an acceptable alternative. The open points are narrow and concrete: the citation wording that separates B010 from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, the allocation of names and the 2016 overlap for B047, and the weight of the pairing-mechanism question for B051. I note that I am among the four B010 supporters and have tried to describe the B047 and B051 positions in their supporters' own terms.
